V-M-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-RUNTIME.Scenario: Lifecycle, capability authorization, state recovery, RPC, and typed-event acceptance suites pass without browser, model, or UI special cases in the kernel.
V-M-KERNEL-CAPABILITY-RUNTIME.TraceAssertion: Event subscribers cannot determine an RPC result, trace context does not confer authority, and durable event delivery never silently downgrades.

V-M-REFERENCE-PROVING-SLICE.Scenario: S0 and S1 compose replaceable reference plugin families through public kernel contracts and preserve state while replacing runtime identity and authority across restart.
V-M-REFERENCE-PROVING-SLICE.TraceAssertion: The proving path reports separate RPC and event outcomes and remains runnable as a single host-level scenario.

V-M-GRACE-CONTROL-LAYER.Scenario: Context, graph, verification routing, active bundle identities, statuses, assertions, and scopes are accepted by GRACE 4.0.4.
V-M-GRACE-CONTROL-LAYER.TraceAssertion: Spec approval and plan approval remain distinct, and approved plans are never mutated in place.

V-M-CI-BASELINE.Scenario: Repository-owned local CI runs pinned source and correctness gates, architecture-security checks, and permanent S0/S1 proving evidence; PR and master workflows remain thin hosted orchestration.
V-M-CI-BASELINE.TraceAssertion: Every required workflow job calls the same local runner, kernel dependency direction remains outward-only, and local evidence is not promoted to an unobserved GitHub run.

V-M-PERSISTENCE-RECOVERY.Scenario: Production SQLite state and outbox survive process termination at commit, delivery, migration, uninstall, job, and blob temporary-write boundaries; restart reconstructs state, pending delivery, journal continuity, interrupted jobs, and verified content-addressed blobs.
V-M-PERSISTENCE-RECOVERY.TraceAssertion: State and pending outbox records commit atomically, event identity and causal metadata survive journal replay, audit records remain metadata-only, backups restore into a validated fresh profile, and recovery never upgrades an interrupted job to Completed.

V-M-EXTERNAL-PLUGIN-BOUNDARY.Scenario: One unchanged reference consumer executes against builtin Rust, supervised native process, and sandboxed WASM Component providers with identical observable capability, state, and event semantics. Hostile WASM and malformed IPC traffic are contained deterministically.
V-M-EXTERNAL-PLUGIN-BOUNDARY.TraceAssertion: Process isolation and WASM sandboxing never replace broker authorization, host handles are runtime-scoped and attenuated, WASM instances hold zero ambient WASI permissions, and installation state survives external provider restart without inheriting live authority.

V-M-OPERABILITY-COMPATIBILITY-UPGRADE.Scenario: Kernel evaluates contract compatibility without granting authority, rejects incompatible updates before switch, isolates staged migrations on copy, validates pre-switch health, switches active revision atomically, rolls back to LastKnownGood upon post-switch failure, quarantines crashing plugins, executes safe mode with core composition, bisects candidate sets, gathers payload-free telemetry, and flags diagnostic gaps.
V-M-OPERABILITY-COMPATIBILITY-UPGRADE.TraceAssertion: Staged updates possess zero authority prior to switch, migrations execute on copy, failed validation never replaces LastKnownGood, rollback mints fresh RuntimeId without grant inheritance, and unprovable external side effects remain explicitly Incomplete without synthetic retry.

V-M-BROWSER-CONTRACT-ENGINE-SPIKE.Scenario: Browser Contract v1 compiles without engine types, enforces strict separation between observation and mutation, validates revision-scoped element references, and prevents browser events from dispatching commands. Executable engine spike navigates deterministic local pages, extracts accessibility trees, executes form interactions, proves context profile isolation, and verifies host survival under child process crash.
V-M-BROWSER-CONTRACT-ENGINE-SPIKE.TraceAssertion: Observation and query authority cannot navigate or act, stale element references are rejected, browser events report facts rather than commands, profile storage remains strictly partitioned across contexts, and child crash containment preserves host and installation state.

V-M-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER-PROCESS.Scenario: Supervised native browser provider process executes all 12 browser capability contracts, enforces strict authority separation and document revision-scoped CAS validation, provides bounded accessibility tree snapshots and content-addressed visual capture streaming, isolates cookie and local storage partitions across contexts, terminates multi-process CEF process trees automatically via Windows Job Object containment upon host close, and successfully passes the end-to-end S2 proving slice.
V-M-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER-PROCESS.TraceAssertion: Process tree containment guarantees zero orphaned renderer/GPU helper processes, CAS generation reservation prevents stale action execution, capability authorizations are default-deny and verified at the native IPC boundary, and proving slice S2 provides durable verification parity.
